panels.description: Origin requests actually reaching the app, by HTTP status. Cloudflare cache hits never appear here, so a jump can mean either more traffic or fewer edge hits.
panels.title: Request rate by status

panels.description: Full server-side latency including every middleware layer. This is the number that matches what a user feels; the inner histogram below excludes user_session and postgres_logging.
panels.title: Request latency (end-to-end)

panels.description: Handler time only. Routes are the matched path pattern, so cardinality stays bounded; unmatched requests bucket under <other>.
panels.title: p95 latency by route (top 10)

panels.description: The tail. A regression that shows here but not in p95 is usually a subset of requests stalling, not everything getting slower.
panels.title: p99 latency by route (top 10)

panels.description: The gap between the two histograms is time spent in the layers outside `metrics`: user_session, postgres_logging, tracking_analytics, language, trace_id, default_no_store.
panels.title: Middleware overhead per request

panels.description: Concurrent requests being served. Little's law: this ≈ request rate × mean latency, so it climbs when requests start waiting on something.
panels.title: Requests in flight

panels.description: Time blocked in bb8's get(). Invisible in every other metric: a request waiting here burns no CPU and holds no connection. If this tracks the request-latency tail, the pool is the bottleneck.
panels.title: Connection acquire wait

panels.description: direct = a connection was free; waited = had to block; timed_out = gave up after connection_timeout.
panels.title: Checkouts by outcome

panels.description: Fraction of checkouts that blocked. Rising here is the earliest sign the pool is under-provisioned or too cold.
panels.title: Checkouts that had to wait

panels.description: total vs idle vs the configured ceiling (DB_CONNECTIONS). total − idle is what is actually checked out right now.
panels.title: Pool connections

panels.description: max_lifetime/idle_timeout closes mean the pool is recycling connections; every close forces a fresh Postgres handshake on some later request.
panels.title: Connection churn

panels.description: How long a single task poll occupies a worker. Long polls block every other task on that worker, which shows up as latency even when CPU looks idle.
panels.title: Task poll time, p99.9

panels.description: The histogram only samples a fraction of polls; the runtime's own counter is the true rate.
panels.title: Task poll rate

panels.description: A large max/min spread means work is unevenly distributed across workers.
panels.title: Mean poll duration

panels.description: Busy time as a fraction of available worker capacity. High latency with a low value here means waiting, not computing.
panels.title: Worker saturation

panels.description: Backlog waiting to be scheduled. A growing blocking queue means spawn_blocking work is starved of threads.
panels.title: Queue depths

panels.description: Forced yields mean tasks are exhausting their budget (long CPU-bound sections); overflow means local queues are spilling to the global one; noop parks are wakeups with no work found.
panels.title: Scheduler activity

panels.description: Jobs waiting per pipeline stage. Sustained growth means the renderer is not keeping up with uploads.
panels.title: Render queue depth

panels.description: download / render / encode / upload.
panels.title: Stage duration, p95

panels.description: gsfs is the primary; backblaze is the fallback; failed means neither served the blob.
panels.title: Map downloads by source

panels.description: Files staged on disk waiting to be shipped. Should hover near zero.
panels.title: Pumper backlog

panels.description: Re-authorization is only triggered by a failed download, so anything sustained here means B2 is unhappy. Stays empty while GSFS serves every blob — the B2 path is a fallback that is currently never taken.
panels.title: Backblaze auth calls

panels.description: Sawtooth resets are process restarts — the quickest way to line a behaviour change up against a deploy.
panels.title: Uptime (drops mark restarts/deploys)
